# Mark Cuban Compared Nvidia to a Dot-Com-Era IPO Machine "Funding Everyone and Anyone." Here's What That Means for AI Stocks.

Motley Fool - 14 minutes ago

## Key Points [...] Cuban's warning is not a blanket argument against AI stocks. Large cloud providers and profitable AI chip and networking players can fund much of their spending from existing operations. A slowdown in data center construction could reduce their free cash flow, orders, or valuations, but it would not immediately threaten their ability to operate.

The warning matters most for companies that need regular outside funding to keep expanding. Specialized cloud operators face greater risk.

items.raw_snippet:
Capital raised and valuation are separate economic questions. A company that raised $1 billion and is marked at $50 billion does not “owe” investors $50 billion; investors hold an appreciated equity stake. Raising $10 billion is not economically equivalent to losing $10 billion.

The more interesting pattern

Once the misleading “payback” framing is stripped away, the chart reveals something more consequential: AI is increasingly separating into two very different capital regimes. [...] On the other side are application-layer and vertical companies. Cursor, ElevenLabs, Suno, Harvey, Perplexity and especially Midjourney convert comparatively modest external capital into substantial revenue far more quickly. Harvey’s additional $200 million financing in March at an $11 billion valuation is one illustration of how vertical AI can attract substantial valuations without needing frontier-lab-scale infrastructure financing. [...] sits at the efficient end. SpaceX announced a $60 billion all-stock acquisition in June, expected to close in the third quarter; describing the company as “on its way” into that structure is accurate. ElevenLabs had raised more than $781 million and surpassed $500 million ARR by May, producing a ratio near 1.6 years. items.raw_snippet: # Salesforce to hire 2,000 for AI product sales, says CEO Marc Benioff. 1. Salesforce to Hire 2,000 Salespeople for AI Expansion. 2. Salesforce’s AI Push Following 2022 Layoffs. * CEO Marc Benioff announced that Salesforce will add 2,000 new employees to sell its artificial intelligence products, doubling initial hiring plans. * The new sales team will help promote Salesforce’s upcoming AI software, including the second version of its Agentforce platform, launching in February 2025. * Following layoffs in 2022, Salesforce is now focusing on growing its AI capabilities and expanding its workforce. **Salesforce is set to hire 2,000 new salespeople to focus on selling artificial intelligence (AI) products, doubling its initial hiring plans as the company prepares to launch its next-generation AI agent software in February 2025.**. Salesforce plans to hire 2,000 new salespeople to focus on selling artificial intelligence (AI) products as the company planning to expand its AI offerings. ### Salesforce to Hire 2,000 Salespeople for AI Expansion. A month ago, Benioff mentioned that Salesforce would hire 1,000 new salespeople for AI roles. Salesforce aims to make AI a key part of its product lineup, with AI tools to help sales teams, marketers, and customer service agents do their jobs more efficiently. The new salespeople will help introduce and sell Salesforce’s latest AI technology, including the upcoming second version of its Agentforce platform. This software is designed to create AI-powered agents to handle complex tasks, like answering questions in Salesforce’s Slack app using all available data. Benioff is very excited about Salesforce’s potential for AI. In a recent interview, he shared, *“I’ve never been more excited about anything at Salesforce, maybe in my career.”* He added that he expects the company to have over a billion AI agents within the next year. ### Salesforce’s AI Push Following 2022 Layoffs. Salesforce’s move into AI comes after the company laid off over 7,000 employees in 2022. With its new AI agents and expanded sales team, Salesforce is aiming to become a major player in the AI industry. ### Stay on top of crypto news, get daily updates in your inbox. ## - The Crypto newsletter that keeps you ahead -.

items.raw_snippet: * English Content Revolut founder set to launch venture capital fund powered by artificial intelligence. # Revolut founder set to launch venture capital fund powered by artificial intelligence. Revolut founder Nik Storonsky is set to launch his own venture capital fund, powered by artificial intelligence. The new venture — dubbed QuantumLight Capital — will be worth around $200 million, with funds supplied by Storonsky and other investors, Forbes reported on Tuesday. “We are built as a technology company by a team of tech unicorn founders, quant traders, AI scientists and engineers,” the QuantumLight website states. The fund will identify investment opportunities using a machine called Aleph as its “proprietary quantitative decision engine.”. According to Forbes, QuantumLight will be focused mainly on Series B and Series C rounds, based on software which eliminates “human judgement.” Storonsky argues that the model is designed to eliminate the clubby world of venture capital, where decisions are made through a crowd mentality. The neobank founder has spent the last year building a team of data scientists and engineers to browse LinkedIn, corporate filings and other public databases in order to identify fast-growing startups. He will also hire in a CEO to head up the fund, according to the Forbes report. The move comes at a time of global expansion for Revolut. In recent months it has acquired banking licenses in at least 10 European countries as it has touted adding new products to it roster, such as home loans and buy-now-pay-later. It has also tussled with UK regulators over anti-money laundering requirements for its crypto products. It is still on the Financial Conduct Authority’s so-called temporary register, alongside crypto custodian Copper and three other firms. The register is a stopgap measure the FCA created after missing an earlier deadline to green-light companies’ operations. Their fate remains uncertain, but without full registration they could in theory be forced to stop crypto-related activities in the UK. ##### Relative altcoin weakness masks early internal rotation. ##### Block Scholes crypto options data comes to Bloomberg terminal to ‘Build Bridge’ for financial institutions. ##### China’s solar energy set to overtake coal, but new coal rush threatens ‘historic’ shift.

* Startup E42 creates marketplace for companies to hire artificial intelligence workers. # Startup E42 creates marketplace for companies to hire AI workers. Studies show by 2026 at least 50 per cent of the enterprise workforce will be AI workers. Studies show by 2026 at least 50 per cent of the enterprise workforce will be AI workers **Shutterstock**. Enterprises and companies across sectors will soon be able to recruit artificial intelligence (AI) workers from the internet, just like hiring personnel from employment portals. AI focussed startup E42 has announced it is setting up a marketplace for AI workers where companies can explore and hire AI bots offering basic services such as receptionist, customer care executives, selling agents to more complex ones such HR executives, IT operations manager, lab assistants, analysts among others. Animesh Samuel, co-founder and CEO, E42, said at the launch of the platform, various studies show by 2026 at least 50 per cent of the enterprise workforce will be AI workers, opening up a $800 billion industry business opportunity. The aim of the E42 marketplace would be to create a platform like Naukri or Monster but for hiring AI workers. E42 co-founder and CTO Sanjeev Menon said that AI workers today are able to connect various data sources and generate insights on various interactions. Menon said that being a no-code natural language processing (NLP) platform, there is flexibility for E42 platform to customise the AI workers as per the requirement of the enterprise. They are able to add their subject matter expertise into the platform and create AI workers to automate specific workers within the organisation,” Menon said. E42 has already seen more than 50 per cent of the customer interaction happening for some of the companies through AI and Menon said that this is expected to increase as AI adoption makes a transition from an aspirational aspect to an essential utility for companies. ‘Islamabad Accord’ envisages ceasefire then final agreement, Reuters source says; ceasefire could reopen Hormuz immediately; final deal in 15–20 days with nuclear curbs, sanctions relief. * ## SC orders CBI probe into allegations against Arunachal CM over public contracts allotment. * ## Any US-Iran ceasefire must ensure free passage through Hormuz, UAE says.
